description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

RTX is hiring an early-career Software Engineer to develop and support safety-of-life air traffic control systems. The role focuses on supporting, designing, developing, integrating, and testing operational software components, improving software processes, and collaborating with engineering teams and stakeholders.
Software Engineer I making guided fixes and enhancements to Air Traffic Control product-line software, updating process documentation, and participating in Agile delivery

Responsibilities:
• Make complex fixes to solve problems or create significant enhancements with guidance from Subject Matter Experts in the Air Traffic Control (ATC) Product Line software
• Update SW process documentation and work instructions needed to meet ATS SED’s high maturity level software engineering standards and processes
• Participate in agile processes and procedures to improve daily standups, sprint planning, sprint feature development, retrospectives, back log grooming and story pointing while using Atlassian tool suite
• Work with the software team and leadership in a highly collaborative team environment, requiring frequent multi-level communication with other engineering domain team members, program management and external stakeholders

Requirements:
• Requires a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in the STEM areas of Computer Science or Software Engineering
• Experience in a Unix/Linux development environment and command line usage
• Strong software experience with  C, C++ or JAVA programming languages
• U.S. citizenship is absolutely required, as only U.S. citizens are authorized to access information under these programs/contracts

Preferred:
• Experience with Agile methodologies and GIT
• Proficiency with scripting languages such as Bash and Python
• Intern experience in Software Engineering which includes exposure to various phases of the software development lifecycle
• Good communication skills, both written and verbal, including formal presentations
